punchline: Rich dad's first money lesson for two nine-year-olds was to cut their pay to zero.
thirty_sec: When Robert Kiyosaki was about nine, he and his friend Mike asked Mike's dad to teach them about money. He had them dust store shelves for a tiny wage, and when Robert complained, he cut the pay to nothing. Then the boys noticed the store was throwing out comic books. They turned them into a reading library for kids that made money even when they weren't there. That became the core idea of Rich Dad Poor Dad.
question: Is there something you own that you've always called an asset but that actually costs you money every month?
